newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Olympics-Sydney unveils three mascots for 2000 Games.
newsitem.headline: Olympics-Sydney unveils three mascots for 2000 Games.

text.p: The organising committee for the Sydney Olympics on Friday unveiled three official mascots for the 2000 Games, each based on a native Australian animal and one the first female character used at a summer Olympics.
Games organisers however shied away from using two of the best-known Australian native animals, the kangaroo and the koala.
Inflatable kangaroos on bicycles used during the closing ceremony at the Atlanta Olympics last year drew widespread criticism in Australia.

The mascots -- "Millie" the echidna, "Olly" the kookaburra and "Syd" the platypus -- were named to represent earth, air and water, said a spokesman for the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG).
The echidna, or spiny ant-eater, and the platypus, an amphibious creature with a flat beak and a beaver-like tail, are both monotremes, or egg-laying mammals.
The kookaburra is the world's largest kingfisher and is known for a call which sounds like human laughter.
"We wanted to get across the message that there are other unique fauna in Australia apart from kangaroos and koalas," the SOCOG spokesman said.
"The duck-billed platypus and the echidna are also the only two monotremes in the world."
The spokesman said SOCOG also felt it was important at least one of the mascots -- in this case Millie -- was female.

Mascots at previous summer Games dating back to "Waldi" the dachshund at the 1972 Munich Games had been either clearly male or androgynous characters such as the computer-generated "Izzy" used with mixed success in Atlanta last year.
"Given it was a family of mascots we felt we needed at least one female," the spokesman said.
